analysis.title: Globant SA (GLOB): Demand headwinds in Middle East offset underlying progress in AI service initiatives
key_insights: GS expects GLOB to be range bound after a narrowed 2026 outlook. Progress on AI initiatives is offset by incremental demand weakness in the Middle East.
3Q26 revenue was $611mn, in line with the Street at $613mn and GS at $611mn (-1.0% Y/Y). Non-GAAP EPS was $1.48 vs Street $1.50 and GS $1.49.
Non-GAAP gross margin of 36.8% beat the Street at 36.7% and GS at 34.0%. Non-GAAP operating margin of 14.1% matched the Street at 14.0% and was below GS at 14.7%.
FY26 revenue guidance was lowered to $2.429-$2.437bn (-1.1% to -0.7% Y/Y) from -1.1% to +0.3% Y/Y. It sits below GS and the Street at $2.446bn. FX is a +0.7% tailwind, unchanged.

FY26 adjusted operating margin guidance was kept at 13.5%-14.5%, against GS at 14.5% and the Street at 13.9%. FY26 adjusted EPS guidance moved to $5.77-$5.87 from $5.75-$6.15, against GS prior $6.00 and the Street $5.89.
4Q26 revenue guidance is $596-$604mn with neutral FX, below GS prior at $613mn and the Street at $612mn.
The AI Pods business is now expected to reach exit run-rate ARR of $130mn by end-2026, up from $110mn. GS sees a large pipeline of AI-led project work over the long run.

GS thinks it may take several quarters for the end markets and clients where Globant is most exposed to return to a favorable growth profile. Investor expectations were low going into the print given macro pressure and Middle East exposure.
GS sees the results as broadly neutral for its IT Services coverage.
GS cut 2026/27/28 EPS to $5.85/$6.70/$7.15 from $6.00/$6.65/$6.75. The changes reflect lower revenue, higher margin and a lower share count. 2027/28 revenue estimates fall 2.9% and 4.3%.
Estimate cuts by vertical are concentrated in 2027/28. Travel & Hospitality 2027E drops to $279mn from $299mn, and Media and Entertainment 2027E to $513mn from $524mn.
The 12-month price target was cut to $50 from $52, based on 7X P/E (down from 8X on lower peer multiples). The stock is rated Neutral, with $39.98 implying 25.1% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS cuts its target to $50 from $52 on a lower peer multiple (7X P/E vs 8X) with estimates little changed. Middle East demand weakness and a lowered FY26 revenue guide are balanced against AI Pods ARR growth.

earnings_insights: GLOB 3Q26 reported revenue $611mn vs Street consensus $613mn (Visible Alpha) and GS estimate $611mn, -1.0% Y/Y.
GLOB 3Q26 non-GAAP EPS from continuing operations reported $1.48 vs Street consensus $1.50 and GS estimate $1.49.
GLOB 3Q26 non-GAAP gross margin reported 36.8% vs Street 36.7% and GS estimate 34.0%. Non-GAAP operating margin reported 14.1% vs Street 14.0% and GS estimate 14.7%.

GLOB FY26 guidance: revenue $2.429-$2.437bn (previously -1.1% to +0.3% Y/Y), adjusted operating margin 13.5%-14.5% (maintained), adjusted EPS $5.77-$5.87 (previously $5.75-$6.15). Street consensus is $2.446bn, 13.9% and $5.89.
GLOB 4Q26 company guidance for revenue is $596-$604mn vs Street consensus $612mn and prior GS estimate $613mn.
GS revised FY26/27/28 non-GAAP EPS estimates to $5.85/$6.70/$7.15 from $6.00/$6.65/$6.75 and revenue to $2,433mn/$2,452mn/$2,530mn from $2,446mn/$2,526mn/$2,644mn.
risk_factors: Upside risks: earlier-than-expected recovery in discretionary spending, increased demand for AI-related projects, stronger-than-expected deal conversion.
Downside risks: demand slowdown in unique verticals (media, sports and other entertainment), further revenue slowdown, dilutive M&A.
Macro uncertainty is pressuring some of Globant's verticals, and recovery in its key end markets may take several quarters.
geopolitical: Demand weakness in the Middle East is cited as an incremental headwind to Globant, which has meaningful exposure to the region.

tension_points.theme: Globant AI pods vs Middle East
tension_points.bull_case: AI Pods exit run-rate ARR is expected to reach $130mn by end-2026, up from $110mn. GS sees an extensive pipeline of next-generation AI-led project work over the long run.
tension_points.bear_case: Incremental demand weakness in the Middle East and macro pressure on some verticals led to a narrower FY26 outlook, with revenue guidance lowered and 4Q26 guided below the Street.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An earlier-than-expected recovery in discretionary spending, increased demand for AI-related projects, or stronger-than-expected deal conversion would challenge the range-bound view.

theme_stances.key_argument: GS is encouraged by the tailwinds Globant expects from AI Pods, with exit run-rate ARR rising to $130mn from $110mn.
Incremental demand weakness in the Middle East tempers progress and led Globant to narrow its outlook.
